page.overview:
What is One Ring?

The One Ring, also known as the Ruling Ring, Master Ring, Ring of Power, and Isildur's Bane, was among the most powerful artifacts ever created in Middle-earth. It was crafted by the Dark Lord Sauron in the fire of Orodruin (usually known as Mount Doom), about halfway into the Second Age. Sauron's intent was to enhance his own power and exercise control over the other Rings of Power, which had been made by Celebrimbor and the Gwaith-i-Mírdain with Sauron's assistance. In this way, Sauron hoped to gain lordship over the Elves and all other peoples of Middle-earth.

Following the defeat of his master Morgoth at the end of the First Age, Sauron went into hiding. After hiding for about the first 500 years of the Second Age, Sauron made his return to the Middle-earth. Desiring still to gain dominion over it as his master had, Sauron concocted a plan to do so without the need for military action.

To do this, Sauron conceived of a set of magic Rings that he would aid the Elves in forging, and then by way of a singular, more powerful Ring, he would be able to bend the wills of those who wore the Rings to his own. He planned for the Rings to be in the hands of as many powerful, influential Elves as could be managed, and by enslaving their wills to his own, he could thereby rule the Elves. Once they were under his sway, he assumed that the other peoples of Middle-earth could be either persuaded to join him or be conquered with relative ease. As such, he spent a significant amount of time amongst the Elves, taking on the fair guise of Annatar, Lord of Gifts, to deceive them into trusting him before eventually instructing them to create the Rings. After the sixteen planned upon Rings (The Seven & The Nine) had been forged, Sauron returned to Mordor (he had established it as his stronghold hundreds of years before) around the year SA 1600, and within the Sammath Naur (usually called the Cracks of Doom) upon Mount Doom, fashioned the One Ring, though the Elves were unaware of his deception at that point.

Sauron had known since the beginning of his endeavor that, to exercise control over the other Rings, the One would have to be an object of surpassing potency. To give the One the power necessary to fulfill its function, he concentrated within it the greater part of his own fëa (soul). In this way, Sauron's fate became bound to that of the Ring. If it were damaged or destroyed, so too would be Sauron's strength and power, and he would be reduced to a mere shadow, making this one of the most significant flaws of the One Ring's design. Another flaw of the One Ring was that if another individual wielded it, they could inherit all of the power Sauron had passed to the Ring and, as such, would become the ruler of the Ring.
